quotes.text: One good meal is a good start. A hundred of them is a habit.
Nobody eats well by accident. It is built from small choices, repeated on ordinary days.
A plan does not need to be perfect. It needs to survive a busy Wednesday.
Consistency is not doing everything right. It is doing something right on most days.
A habit is a decision you no longer have to make. Choose the ones worth automating.
What you do on an average day matters far more than what you do on your best one.
Tiny changes look invisible on the day you make them and obvious a year later.
The best way of eating is the one you will still follow when you are tired, busy and bored.
Make the good choice the easy choice, and it will happen without a speech.
Slow progress is still progress, and it has a habit of lasting.
Good habits rarely feel dramatic. They feel like Tuesday.
Change one thing this week. Let it become boring. Then change the next.
The goal is not to be strict. The goal is to be steady.
You do not need a fresh start on Monday. You can begin again with the very next meal.
Willpower gets tired by evening. Habits do not. Set the day up so it needs less of the first.
Every meal you log is a small act of paying attention, and attention is where change begins.
Little by little, the plate you fill on autopilot becomes the plate you would have chosen anyway.
There is nothing glamorous about eating well every day, which is exactly why it works.
A habit is only a series of small yeses, said often enough that they stop being hard.
Start so small it feels silly. Silly is easy to repeat.
A stumble is not a reset. It is a Tuesday, and Wednesday is coming.
Repeat the good day. Repeat it again. That is most of the secret.
Progress is rarely a straight line, but it is almost always a lot of small ones.
The person who eats well tomorrow is built by the person who decided to try today.
Do not wait to feel motivated. Do the small thing and let motivation catch up.
Two glasses of water, one more vegetable, a slower dinner. Ordinary things, done for years, are extraordinary.
If you can keep it up on a bad day, it is a habit. If you can only do it on a good day, it is a mood.
A system works even on the days you feel nothing. A resolution needs you to feel strong.
You are always one meal away from a better day.
The next choice is the only one you can actually make. Make it a decent one.
Habits are how a good intention gets a job.
It is easier to add one good thing than to remove ten bad ones. Start by adding.
The days you least feel like it are the days the habit is quietly being built.
Eating well is less about willpower and more about what you keep in the kitchen.
Your kitchen shelf is a decision you made in advance, on behalf of a tired future you.
Make tomorrow’s breakfast easy tonight and morning-you will be grateful.
Ten minutes of preparation on Sunday can quietly fix five weekday evenings.
The habit you repeat is the habit that wins, whatever you intended.
Doing it imperfectly on Thursday beats planning it perfectly for Monday.
You do not have to feel ready. You only have to begin with what you have.
A good routine is not a cage. It is the railing that lets you move quickly in the dark.
Keep the promise small enough that you can keep it on the worst day.
Long streaks are made of ordinary mornings.
Track it, notice it, adjust it, repeat it. There is no secret step five.
If it takes a heroic effort, it is not a habit yet. Make it smaller.
What you repeat on Tuesdays and Thursdays shapes you more than what you do on holidays.
Success at eating well is mostly deciding what you will do before the hungry moment arrives.
It is fine to be bad at this for a while. Everyone who is good at it once was.
The habit does not have to be exciting. It only has to be there tomorrow.
The best habits are the ones that stop feeling like habits.
Eat well often enough and it stops being a project. It becomes a personality.
Do the small thing daily, and one day you will look up and find it was never small.
Give a new habit at least a month before you decide whether it suits you.
The distance between where you are and where you want to be is measured in Tuesdays.
Build the day so that the good choice takes no argument.
Persistence is just a quiet word for showing up again.
No one ever changed their health in a day, but plenty have in a year of ordinary ones.
Let your default be the good thing, and keep your effort for the exceptions.
Each time you pick the better option, the next time gets a little easier to pick.
A small habit kept beats a big plan abandoned.
